name: Phebe N. Novakovic

career.organization: White House Office of Management and Budget
career.title: Deputy associate director, overseeing defense and intelligence budgets
Special assistant to Defense Secretary William Cohen and Deputy Secretary John Hamre
Vice President of Strategic Planning, then Senior Vice President of Planning and Development
Executive Vice President, Marine Systems Group

background_rationale: After CIA and Pentagon budget and policy roles, she joined General Dynamics as its top strategic planner and ran its Marine Systems shipbuilding group and then the whole company as COO before becoming CEO.

notable.summary: Taking over after a roughly $2 billion write-down tied to past IT acquisitions, Novakovic halted new acquisitions, cut headquarters staff and redirected cash to dividends and share buybacks.
General Dynamics pulled out of bidding for the U.S. Air Force T-X trainer jet program, which Fortune estimated at $30-40 billion.
General Dynamics completed its $9.7 billion acquisition of IT services firm CSRA, combining it with General Dynamics Information Technology.
Novakovic said the combined CSRA and GDIT would offer competitive solutions to customers and attractive free cash flow and returns on capital for investors.

personal_story.hook: Phebe Novakovic went from CIA operations officer to Pentagon aide to running one of America's biggest defense contractors.
personal_story.summary: Novakovic is the daughter of a Serbian immigrant who served as a lieutenant colonel in U.S. Air Force military intelligence, and she attended an Episcopal boarding school in San Antonio. She majored in government and German at Smith College, graduating in 1979, and started out analyzing weapons systems for a small Washington-area contractor. She joined the CIA as an operations officer in 1983, later earned a Wharton MBA, and spent the 1990s at the White House budget office overseeing defense and intelligence spending before becoming a special assistant to the Secretary of Defense. In 2001 she moved to General Dynamics as its strategic planner, ran its shipbuilding group, and became CEO in January 2013.
